sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices across all products, and the three years to FY2025 show a -5.3% CAGR [D274][P47][D844].
Note that the table's revenue is a later recast, not the figure first reported: FY2025 is $51.8 billion here against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10][R1].
Crude oil is the largest revenue line at 66.3% of revenue in FY2025, and it grew only 0.1% that year [D551][D552].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of revenue and contributed 5.7pp of the 4.9% revenue growth in FY2025 [D382][D384][D342].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% while revenue rose 4.9%, so there was no operating leverage in FY2025 [D343][D342].
Basic EPS fell 18.7%, faster than net income, because the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D344][D343][D356].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, after a 3.9pp decline in FY2024 [D351][D317].
DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025, mainly from the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22].
Production and operating expenses rose $1.6 billion, including $216 million of restructuring severance, and purchased commodities rose $2.3 billion [P24][P25].
The effective tax rate rose to 36.9%, so net margin sits well below the operating result [D332].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 1.52x of FY2022 [F59][F20][D333][D226].
Operating cash flow fell slightly in FY2025 on lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6].
Free cash flow is only reported to FY2022, when it was $18.2 billion, a 23.1% margin [F73][D223].
Capex was 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 and 1.35x D&A, so capital intensity was rising into the acquisition years [D222][D228].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in FY2025, the 100th percentile of six energy peers against a -7.7% peer median [D337][D338][D850][D851].
In FY2025 the company spent $12.6 billion on capital and investments, $5.0 billion on buybacks, $4.0 billion on dividends and $0.9 billion on debt retirement [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the stated 30% framework [D339][F59][P31].
Return on average equity was 12.4%, below the 14.9% peer median and the 33rd percentile of six peers [D341][D853][D852].
The revenue basis break is the main data-quality flag: every year in the table is a recast, so growth and margins mix presentations [R1][F10][X10].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized commodity prices, a one-period decline [R2][D274][P47].
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of consolidated revenue in FY2025, so they cannot be added [R4].
FY2017 SG&A was later reported as $427 million against $561 million first reported, a low-severity recast [R3][X42].
Watch net margin against the 17.9% window median; a print above it would reverse the FY2025 decline [D831][F30].
Watch net cash as a share of revenue against the 12.1% FY2025 level, with the $5 billion disposition target as the swing factor [D338][P32].
Watch the diluted share count against 1,253.4 million; further growth would keep EPS falling faster than net income [X131][D356].
